title: Why freezing people take off their clothes 🥶
subject: hypothermia
description:
Would you notice it happening to you? 👇

Paradoxical undressing is a real effect of severe hypothermia: as the body freezes, people can feel hot and take off their clothes. A Berlin forensic study of 69 deaths found it in 25% of cases, along with "terminal burrowing".

Sources: Rothschild & Schneider 1995, International Journal of Legal Medicine ("Terminal burrowing behaviour, a phenomenon of lethal hypothermia", Free University of Berlin); Lavezzi et al., AAFS 2006 (Cook County Medical Examiner); New Scientist via Deseret News ("Strange but true", 2007)
tags: why do freezing people take off clothes
what happens when you freeze to death

scenes.text: Freezing to death, you could suddenly feel hot and undress.
Below 35 degrees Celsius, tiny muscles clamp your skin's blood vessels to hold heat in.
When they tire, warm blood floods the skin, and your brain reads it as burning heat.
In Berlin, doctors reviewed 69 hypothermia deaths. A quarter of the victims had undressed.
Most were found squeezed under beds or behind wardrobes. Doctors call it terminal burrowing.
The brain stem seems to run it on autopilot, after clear thinking shuts down.
